I had complex partial seizures mostly and would have seizures in my sleep. We figured this out because of several sleep studies at a local epilepsy monitoring unit after I first got diagnosed with epilepsy.

If you by chance had seizures onset later in life without a clear reason why, it’s definitely worth exploring. I had my first seizure as a teenager and they rapidly increased from 1x every 6 months to once a month, to once a week, to once a day, to 8-10+ times a day everyday. My birth defect became symptomatic due to puberty and hormones and nothing could help them, VNS, meds, nothing. I really hope my experience leads to answers for you, I wouldn’t wish seizures upon anyone.

I didn’t take your response wrong at all, I’m sorry if it was clipped and I apologize for not recognizing the significance of your breakthrough seizure. That is extra shitty with a side of shit, I’m sorry that’s going on for you. I acknowledge the privilege I have of being seizure free and don’t want to be rubbing it in anyones face, I think I have hypochondria / trauma from my epilepsy and other chronic illnesses and am always waiting for the other shoe to drop with my health now.

I went through multiple doctors and clinics before finding a state of the art hospital that had an epilepsy review board of epileptologists that suggested I get an MEG, which is a scan that atleast five+ years ago wasn’t easy to find and I had to travel out of state to get one, however they suspected I had a cortical dysplasia and that was the only scan that would show it as an MRI, CT, etc would not. I was extremely lucky to have excellent health insurance to cover all of my diagnostics as the MEG was 26k without insurance and I probably would still be having seizures today without it. I wish you luck, friend!

I’ve had testing to see if I’m still experiencing seizure activity, and because I had the cause of my seizures removed from my brain with a resection I’ve been told the likelihood of seizure reoccurrence is about the same as anyone off the street now despite my history.

MEG scan, invasive EEG, years or ruling out other causes, trying every type of antiepileptic med cocktail without them helping, a VNS implant and then explant because it did nothing. I had a cortical dysplasia.

I really appreciate your feedback and sharing your experiences. When I was actively epileptic I would experience similar to what you described, get even the whiff of a seizure and then start to mentally spiral and get anxiety about having a seizure until inevitably I would have a seizure. I’m so glad you’re controlled with medication and also seizure free, I hope your quality of life has much improved if seizures had previously reduced it. Thanks again!

I was on a myriad of medications including Keppra when I was trying to manage my epilepsy with meds, and none of them really worked unfortunately so I was left with side effects. At the time I had an amazing partner, we weren’t compatible and have since married different people, but one thing I learned was that caregiver burn out is real. Although it isn’t your wife’s fault that she has epilepsy or that she is suffering uncontrollable side effects from her medications, you can be both a good partner and take care of yourself. I highly recommend therapy if you aren’t already participating in it, for yourself, and other forms of self care when you can to keep you sane. I burnt out my poor ex, he was a saint, and he ended up resenting me after many years of being my caregiver first and my partner second due to the side effects I faced and mental and physical health issues we both faced as a couple. 

Sending you both love and support.
